paragraphs: R. Chanina bar Chama, the priest.

(a) Apparently he is the unqualified R. Chanina mentioned in the Talmud. According to Rabbenu Chananel, his father Chama was R. Chanina ben Dosa's son; see there. He would regularly return the payment for redeeming a firstborn: Bekhorot 51b. Rabbi ordered that he should preside, but he did not accept because Rabbi Afes was two and a half years older; see there, and Levi. He brought rain for the people of Tzippori; see R. Yehoshua ben Levi above, and you will see that this is mistaken. He disputed with R. Chiyya the Great and said that if Torah were forgotten, he would restore it through his reasoning; see there. He permitted Shmuel’s captive daughters to marry; see R. Shemen bar Abba. He would go with Rabbi to Antoninus and revived the servant whom Antoninus killed: Avodah Zarah, chapter 1, 10b. Antoninus went to Rabbi, found R. Chanina bar Chama, and told him to call his servant. He found that Antoninus had killed him, prayed for him, and revived him. Compare Vayikra Rabbah, section 10, for a different version. He was a physician, as in Chullin, chapter 1, 7b: “No one has ever asked me about a wound from a white mule.” In Yoma 49a he permitted R. Yehoshua ben Levi to take a remedy on the Sabbath. He went with R. Yehoshua ben Levi to a governor, who rose before them and said that their faces were the faces of kings [the Jerusalem Talmud reads “angels”]; see there. “They said concerning him in the West” means R. Chanina: Sanhedrin 17. He would wrap himself and stand toward evening on Sabbath eve, saying, “Come, let us go out to greet Queen Sabbath”: Shabbat 119a. His daughter died, and he did not weep, saying, “Bereavement and blindness”: Shoel, Shabbat 151b. Yevamot 122: R. Chanina said, “Yonatan the demon told me”—Rashi: he was a demon, or expert in them—“They have a shadow, but not a shadow of a shadow.” Gittin 66a has in this matter “R. Chanina said: Yonatan my son taught me: a shadow, etc.” It is a scribal error and should read Yonatan the demon. R. Chanina was eighty years old and would stand on one leg and remove his shoes. He said, “The hot water with which my mother anointed me in childhood has stood me in good stead in old age”: Chullin 24b. He expounded at Tzippori, “He breaks into houses in the dark”; see R. Yosi.

(b) His colleagues were Rabbi's sons, Rabban Gamliel and R. Shimon, and R. Oshaya bar Chama. Shalshelet HaKabbalah, 33b, says his colleagues were our holy Rabbi's sons, namely R. Oshaya, R. Shimon, and Rabban Gamliel; it erred; see under Rabbi. Shalshelet HaKabbalah also writes that he received from Rabbi in 3980, 150 years after the destruction—it should read 152 after the destruction—and then became head; see part 1. Tzemach David lists as his colleagues R. Elazar HaKappar, R. Chiyya, Bar Kappara, Levi, Shmuel's father, and R. Afes; he presided ten years, until 3990. Yuchasin, in Rav Sherira Gaon's name: R. Yannai, R. Yochanan, Resh Lakish, R. Yehoshua ben Levi, and R. Shimon ben Elazar.

(c) They made him a coffin in the marketplace on the intermediate festival days because he was a well-known man: Tosafot, Moed Katan 8b, in the name of Jerusalem Moed Katan, chapter 1, halakhah 6: when R. Chananyah, the rabbis' colleague, died, they made him a coffin in the marketplace. Moed Katan 24a: R. Yochanan tore thirteen garments for him and said, “The man I feared has gone.” See R. Yochanan and what I wrote there. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Elu Metziot: R. Yochanan was going up from Tiberias to Tzippori. He saw a man coming down and asked, “What news in the town?” He answered, “A rabbi has died, and all these groups are attending to him.” R. Yochanan knew it was R. Chanina. He sent for fine Sabbath clothes and tore them. But was it not taught that any tearing not done in the shock of the moment is not a valid tearing? R. Yochanan wished to honor him greatly. We do not know whether this was because he was his teacher or because of the bad tidings.

(d) “R. Abba said: R. Chanina said.” R. Abba bar Kahana, in his name. “R. Abba bar Zavda said: R. Chanina said.” “R. Abba bar Zutra said: R. Chanina said.” “R. Idi said: R. Chanina said.” In R. Acha bar Achvah's name. “R. Ilai said: R. Chanina said”; “R. Ilai said.” R. Chanina ruled at Tzippori. R. Chanina objected to R. Ilai, who said to him, etc. R. Ilai said, “May the Merciful One save us from that opinion.” R. Chanina answered, “On the contrary, may the Merciful One save us from your opinion.” Ilfa said, “We will act like R. Chanina.” “R. Elazar said: R. Chanina said.” “R. Ammi said: R. Chanina probably taught [תר״ח]: Rabbi said”—Bava Batra 130b; Jerusalem Maaserot, chapter 1. “Rav Assi said: R. Chanina said.” “Rav Ashi said: Rabbi said.” Rav Bivi, in his name. R. Berekhiah, in his name. “Rav Dimi said: R. Chanina said.” “Rav Huna said: R. Chanina said.” R. Hamnuna said, “R. Chanina taught me this matter.” Rav Hamnuna the scribe asked him. “R. Zeira said: R. Chanina said”—Shabbat 125b; Gittin 39b, near the end. “Zeiri said: R. Chanina said.” Zeira bar Chinena, in his name. R. Zerika, in his name. And Rav Chaviva. R. Chiyya bar Abba: Yuchasin writes that he was R. Chanina's student; this requires investigation. R. Chiyya bar Adda, in his name. And R. Chiyya bar Mariya. Rav Chelbo. R. Chanin, in his name. R. Chanina the Elder said to him. R. Chanina bar Sisi wished to transmit the Explicit Name to him. And R. Yehudah bar Zevina. R. Yehoshua ben Levi; see above. R. Yochanan, in his name; see above, that he was his colleague. When R. Yochanan went to greet him, he would make a sound before entering. And R. Yonah; R. Yonatan; R. Yonatan ben Akhmai; R. Yonatan ben Elazar. Before R. Yannai. R. Yaakov bar Idi, in his name. R. Yaakov Gevulaya, in his name. R. Yitzchak bar Maryon, in his name. R. Yirmeyah. R. Yishmael son of R. Yosi said, and cursed R. Chanina with askara; see there. In R. Yishmael son of R. Yaakov bar Acha's name. R. Levi, in his name; apparently he was his colleague there. And R. Muna. R. Mana bar Tanchum, in his name. R. Mani said to him. He sent for R. Mana when R. Yehudah Nesia's sister died. In R. Misha's name. And R. Marinos. In Abba Nehorai's name. Ulla bar Yishmael, in his name. Ulla of Caesarea, in his name. Ulla Beraya [ברייה; byname or relationship unresolved], in his name. Ulla, in his name. He permitted Mar Ukva. R. Amram ben Shimon bar Abba said: R. Chanina said. Akavya asked him. R. Pinchas bar Chama, the priest—perhaps his brother. R. Parnakh, in his name. Rav offended him and went to appease him on thirteen eves of Yom Kippur, but he was not appeased: Yoma 87b, beginning. Rambam writes that Rav was his student; Taz, Orach Chayyim, beginning of section 606, writes that he was not his student. Sukkah 43b: “Rav Shmuel said: R. Chanina said.” Rabbah bar Zutra, in his name. And Rabbah bar bar Chana. “R. Romanos said.” Shavchat—whether he was his son requires investigation there. “Rav Shmuel said: R. Chanina said”; see Rav above. Shmuel bar Abba received from him. Rav Shmuel the Elder, his son-in-law, said: R. Chanina said. Rav Shmuel bar Nadav, his son-in-law. R. Shmuel bar Chiyya bar Yehudah, in his name. R. Shmuel bar Natan asked him: R. Chanina said. He permitted R. Shemen bar Abba; see there. Resh Lakish asked him. R. Shimon ben Yosini. In R. Shimon ben Yochai's name: Berakhot 33b. R. Shimon, the scribe of Turbani, asked him. R. Shimon Balluta, in his name. R. Shimon bar Abba, in his name.
